# Install & run

This chapter takes you from a fresh clone to Arisbe running in your browser, and shows where
this book/help lives once the app is up.

## Prerequisites

- **Python 3.12** (Arisbe targets 3.12).
- **[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)** — the project's dependency manager. Install it with
  `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` (macOS/Linux) or see the uv docs for
  other platforms. `uv` creates and manages the virtual environment for you.

That is all you need to run the application. Building the book/help as a PDF or a local site
additionally needs Quarto and a LaTeX toolchain — see *Build the book/help* below.

## Get the code and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mijahauan/Arisbe.git
cd Arisbe
uv sync --extra dev --extra web
```

`uv sync` is exact: the **`web`** extra carries FastAPI and uvicorn (the web viewer and the
route tests need them), and **`dev`** carries the test/quality tooling. If you omit an extra,
`uv sync` will *prune* it — so install both. No manual virtual-environment activation is
needed; prefix commands with `uv run`, or `source .venv/bin/activate` once if you prefer.

## Run the web viewer (the canonical UI)

```bash
uv run uvicorn --app-dir src web_api.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

Then open **<http://localhost:8000/>**. The home page links the three modes:

| Mode | Route | What it is |
|------|-------|------------|
| **Organon** | `/organon` | The archive — browse the corpus and read graphs, read-only. |
| **Ergasterion** | `/ergasterion` | The workshop — draw and compose graphs, practice the rules. |
| **Agon** | `/agon` | The arena — test a graph against a model, play the Endoporeutic Game. |

New to existential graphs? Read **Your first graph** next, then find your **door by
background**.

## Check the install (optional)

```bash
uv run pytest tests/ -q
```

The suite has roughly a thousand passing tests. The mathematical core must always pass; if it
doesn't, something is genuinely wrong rather than flaky.

## Build the book/help

This book is single-sourced from the project's documentation with
[Quarto](https://quarto.org). To render it locally you need Quarto installed, plus a LaTeX
toolchain for the PDF (the same one the Peirce-edition LaTeX export uses; `quarto install
tinytex` provides one).

```bash
# one-time: install Quarto (see quarto.org/docs/get-started) — e.g. on macOS:
brew install quarto

# render the web help (HTML site) into docs/_book/
quarto render docs

# or a specific format
quarto render docs --to pdf
quarto render docs --to epub

# live preview while editing
quarto preview docs
```

The rendered HTML site lands in `docs/_book/`. When that directory exists, the running web
app serves it at **<http://localhost:8000/book/>**, so the book and the in-app help are the
same artifact — never maintained twice.

> The generated outputs (`docs/_book/`, `docs/.quarto/`) are not checked in; run
> `quarto render docs` after pulling to refresh them.
